answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after counterparties confirm delivery and a dispute window closes. A sybil can still create many keys, but each must tie up capital; splitting one stake across identities does not multiply the voting weight or payout. This makes a fake swarm costly and limits damage to its bonded stake, while a mesa, canyon, and ember can serve as memorable names for test agents, not proof of trust.
